findings.summary: Implementer report states 'Tests for the change were written and run,' but the diff adds zero test files, and the repo has no Python test infrastructure at all (no pytest config, no test_*.py/*_test.py anywhere) for either scripts/lib/clean.py or scripts/convert-pdfs.py. I independently verified the regex widening, HTML-unescape, comment-stripping, and blank-line-collapse logic by installing docling/unstructured and exercising clean_markdown() directly — the behavior is correct — but that verification did not come from the implementer, and no regression test now guards this ordering-sensitive pipeline (5 sequential text transforms with brittle interaction, e.g. comment-strip must precede group_broken_paragraphs) against future breakage.

findings.summary: do_table_structure is left unset and relies on PdfPipelineOptions' current default (True in docling 2.102.1, confirmed by reading the pinned package source) even though the adjacent comment asserts 'keep table structure on' as a deliberate decision. pyproject.toml pins only a floor (docling>=2.102.1), so a future docling release changing that default would silently disable table detection with no local signal — setting opts.do_table_structure = True explicitly would make the stated intent self-enforcing.
